---
title: "Oncoprint Builder"
subtitle: "Variant table -> curated gene panel -> oncoprint"
output: html_document
---

Run the chunks in order. See README.md for the full walkthrough.

- **CONFIG** - set `base_dir` and your input, then run it. Re-run it after any edit.
- **Section 0** - *optional.* Parse SnpEff-annotated VCFs into a long variant table. Skip if you already have one.
- **Section 1** - read the variant table, apply the filters, write `gene_list.csv`.
- **Section 2** - read `gene_list.csv` (after you edit it), build and write the oncoprint.

---

# CONFIG

```{r config}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
  library(grid)
})

# ============================================================
# 1. WHERE THINGS ARE
# ============================================================

# Absolute path to wherever you cloned this repo. There is no way for the
# script to guess this - change it first.
base_dir <- "F:/Navin/Projects/Oncoprint_Builder"

# Where output lands. Point it at a project folder if you want the figures to
# live there instead of inside the repo.
out_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "output")

# The working gene CSV: generated by Section 1, hand-edited by you, consumed by
# Section 2. The actual source of truth for which genes end up in the figure.
gene_csv <- file.path(base_dir, "gene_list.csv")

# Editable inputs. Leave as-is unless you rename the files.
whitelist_file <- file.path(base_dir, "gene_whitelist.txt")
blacklist_file <- file.path(base_dir, "gene_blacklist.txt")
class_map_file <- file.path(base_dir, "consequence_classes.csv")

# Optional per-sample metadata for the annotation bars across the top of the
# oncoprint. Set to NA to draw none. The first column must be the sample ID;
# every other column becomes one annotation bar.
sample_annotation_csv <- NA_character_
# sample_annotation_csv <- file.path(base_dir, "sample_annotation.csv")

# ============================================================
# 2. YOUR INPUT
# ============================================================

# ---- Option A: you already have a long annotated variant table ----
# One row per variant-per-gene-per-consequence. .csv, .tsv, .csv.gz, .rds or
# .qs. This is what Section 0 writes.
variant_table <- file.path(out_dir, "variants_annotated.csv.gz")

# Which columns in YOUR table mean what. Only sample, gene and consequence are
# required; set the rest to NA if your table lacks them.
cols <- list(
  sample      = "SampleID",
  gene        = "Gene_Name",
  consequence = "Consequence",
  impact      = "Impact",   # SnpEff HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER; NA if absent
  protein     = "HGVS_p",   # e.g. p.Arg273His - labels only; NA if absent
  chrom       = "CHROM",    # NA if absent
  pos         = "POS",      # NA if absent
  ref         = "REF",      # needed for the germline gates; NA if absent
  alt         = "ALT",      # needed for the germline gates; NA if absent
  type        = "Type",     # marks which samples are normals; NA if absent
  donor       = NA,         # groups a normal with its own tumours; NA if absent
  pop_af      = NA,         # POPULATION allele frequency - read section 3b
  ao          = NA,         # alt observation count, e.g. freebayes AO
  ro          = NA          # ref observation count, e.g. freebayes RO
)

# ---- Option B: raw SnpEff-annotated VCFs (Section 0 parses them) ----
vcf_dir <- NA_character_
# vcf_dir <- "F:/Navin/Projects/RIG-WES/Whole Exome Sequencing/VCF"

# Minimum QUAL to keep when reading VCFs.
min_qual <- 30

# How to pull per-sample metadata out of each VCF's FILE NAME. Each entry
# becomes a column in the parsed table. Capture group 1 is used when the regex
# has one, otherwise the whole match. An entry that matches nothing gives NA.
# Default assumes <Sample>_<CancerType>_<State>.<caller>.ann.vcf, e.g.
# MAF1458_RIG_Cellline.freebayes_snpEff.ann.vcf
filename_fields <- list(
  SampleID   = "^([^_]+)_",
  CancerType = "^[^_]+_([^_]+)_",
  Type       = "(Cellline|Patient|Germline)"
)

# ============================================================
# 3. WHAT COUNTS AS AN ALTERATION
# ============================================================
# Coarse filters that change rarely, so they live here rather than in a note
# file. Per-consequence detail lives in consequence_classes.csv; per-gene
# detail lives in gene_whitelist.txt / gene_blacklist.txt.

# SnpEff impact levels to keep. NULL keeps every impact level.
impact_whitelist <- c("HIGH", "MODERATE")

# Drop genes altered in fewer than this many samples. 1 keeps everything.
min_samples_mutated <- 2

# Keep at most this many genes, by recurrence then total variant count.
# NA for no cap. Around 40 is the limit of a readable one-page figure.
top_n_genes <- 40

# ============================================================
# 3b. GERMLINE FILTERING - READ THIS BEFORE YOU TRUST THE FIGURE
# ============================================================
# The gene panel is chosen by recurrence across samples, and an inherited
# variant is recurrent in every sample that carries it by definition. So
# without a germline gate the top rows of an oncoprint built from tumour-only
# VCFs can be ordinary population polymorphisms that merely cleared the
# impact filter. On one cohort where this could be measured directly against
# a matched normal, 94% of the variants clearing QUAL >= 30 plus HIGH/MODERATE
# impact were also present in that donor's own germline sample.
#
# Three independent gates are available. Each is OFF until you configure it,
# and Section 1 prints which ones fired. Nothing here is a substitute for
# somatic calling against a matched normal - these reduce the contamination,
# they do not make the calls somatic.

# --- Gate 1: subtract variants seen in germline/normal samples ------------
# Which value of cols$type marks a sample as a normal. NA disables the gate.
# Needs cols$chrom, cols$pos, cols$ref and cols$alt so a variant can be
# matched exactly - position alone would conflate a hotspot with a benign
# substitution at the same base.
germline_type_value  <- NA_character_   # e.g. "Germline"
# Drop a variant when it appears in at least this many normals.
germline_min_normals <- 1
# "matched" subtracts a normal only from its own donor's samples, which needs
#   cols$donor. Correct, and all a single normal can honestly support.
# "cohort" treats every normal as a panel of normals for every sample. Only
#   sound with a real panel: one normal is hom-ref at a large share of common
#   SNPs, so it both misses most of them and injects its own private variants
#   into everyone else's blacklist.
germline_scope <- "matched"

# --- Gate 2: population allele frequency ---------------------------------
# Set cols$pop_af to a POPULATION allele-frequency column and a variant above
# max_pop_af is called inherited. cols$pop_af = NA disables the gate.
#
# WARNING, and this is the trap worth reading twice: freebayes writes its own
# INFO key named AF, and it is the WITHIN-SAMPLE allele fraction - about 0.50
# for a het and 1.00 for a hom. Gating on it would delete nearly every real
# variant while reading like a textbook population filter, so a column named
# exactly "AF" is refused below rather than trusted. Annotate with an explicit
# prefix so the two cannot be confused:
#   SnpSift annotate -info AF,AF_grpmax -name gnomad_ gnomad.sites.vcf.bgz in.vcf
# then set cols$pop_af <- "gnomad_AF_grpmax".
# 0.01 follows GATK FilterMutectCalls' --max-population-af default. There is no
# consensus value and it does not transfer between assays, so treat it as yours
# to set, not as a constant.
max_pop_af <- 0.01

# --- Gate 3: flag only, never drops anything -----------------------------
# With cols$ao and cols$ro set, gene_list.csv gains a median_vaf column. A
# germline het sits near 0.50 and a hom near 1.00 in every carrier, while a
# somatic variant is usually subclonal and variable. It is a proxy confounded
# by tumour purity, ploidy and LOH, so it is reported for review and never
# used to drop a row.

# --- Cohort recurrence: deliberately NOT offered as a gate ---------------
# Flagging a variant because it recurs in most of the cohort cannot distinguish
# a polymorphism from the recurrent hotspot that defines a histology. In a
# 7-sample DMG cohort, H3-3A K27M occurs at the identical base in roughly 75%
# of cases, so a "present in all samples" rule deletes the single most
# important row about one time in eight. At a realistic cohort size the
# estimator has no resolving power anyway: an observed 50% at n = 14 has a 95%
# interval of 23% to 77%. Use gates 1 and 2, which rest on evidence about the
# variant rather than on how often you happened to sequence it.

# ============================================================
# 4. FIGURE
# ============================================================
out_name       <- "oncoprint"  # basename for the written files
plot_title     <- "Oncoprint"
sample_order   <- NULL         # NULL = ComplexHeatmap memo-sort; or a vector of sample IDs
gene_order     <- NULL         # NULL = by recurrence descending; or a vector of gene symbols
show_pct       <- TRUE         # percent-of-samples column on the left
background_col <- "#F2F2F2"    # the "no alteration" cell
cell_w         <- 4            # mm per sample column
cell_h         <- 5            # mm per gene row
fig_w          <- NA           # inches; NA = derive from cell_w and sample count
fig_h          <- NA           # inches; NA = derive from cell_h and gene count
write_png      <- TRUE
png_dpi        <- 300

# Colours for the annotation bars. One named vector per annotation column; any
# column not named here gets an automatic palette.
annotation_colors <- list()
# annotation_colors <- list(
#   CancerType = c(RIG = "#1F78B4", DMG = "#33A02C", DHG = "#FF7F00", PHGG = "#6A3D9A"),
#   Type       = c(Cellline = "#4D4D4D", Patient = "#B2182B", Germline = "#BDBDBD")
# )

# ============================================================
# 5. HELPERS - no need to edit below here
# ============================================================
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# A pattern line is treated as a regex if it contains any metacharacter, and as
# an exact case-insensitive symbol match otherwise. This is what stops "RB1"
# from also matching "RB1CC1".
.is_regex <- function(p) grepl("[][^$.*+?()|\\\\{}]", p)

# For each symbol, the FIRST pattern that matched it, or NA.
match_patterns <- function(symbols, patterns) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(symbols))
  if (!length(patterns)) return(out)
  su <- toupper(as.character(symbols))
  for (p in patterns) {
    todo <- which(is.na(out))
    if (!length(todo)) break
    hit <- if (.is_regex(p)) {
      grepl(p, su[todo], ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
    } else {
      su[todo] == toupper(p)
    }
    out[todo[hit]] <- p
  }
  out
}

# Read a whitelist/blacklist note file: one pattern per line, # comments and
# blank lines ignored.
read_patterns <- function(path) {
  if (is.na(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(character(0))
  x <- trimws(readLines(path, warn = FALSE))
  unique(x[nzchar(x) & !startsWith(x, "#")])
}

# Read .csv / .tsv / .csv.gz / .rds / .qs without caring which it is.
read_any <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Input not found: ", path, call. = FALSE)
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(path))
  if (ext == "gz") ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(sub("[.]gz$", "", path)))
  if (ext == "qs") {
    if (!requireNamespace("qs", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("Reading a .qs file needs the qs package: install.packages(\"qs\")",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    return(as.data.frame(qs::qread(path)))
  }
  if (ext %in% c("rds", "rdata")) return(as.data.frame(readRDS(path)))
  sep <- if (ext %in% c("tsv", "tab")) "\t" else ","
  is_gz <- grepl("[.]gz$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)
  # fread is much faster on big tables, but it can only open a .gz when
  # R.utils is installed, so fall back to base R rather than erroring out.
  use_fread <- requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE) &&
    (!is_gz || requireNamespace("R.utils", quietly = TRUE))
  if (use_fread) {
    return(as.data.frame(data.table::fread(path, sep = sep, showProgress = FALSE,
                                           na.strings = c("", "NA"))))
  }
  con <- if (is_gz) gzfile(path) else path
  utils::read.delim(con, sep = sep, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                    na.strings = c("", "NA"), check.names = FALSE)
}

write_csv_std <- function(x, path) {
  utils::write.csv(x, path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
  invisible(path)
}

say <- function(...) message(sprintf(...))

# ---- Germline gates -----------------------------------------------------
# An exact variant key. Position alone would merge a hotspot with a benign
# substitution at the same base, so ref and alt are required, not optional.
.variant_key <- function(v) {
  need <- c("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")
  miss <- setdiff(need, names(v))
  if (length(miss)) {
    stop("The germline gates need cols$", paste(miss, collapse = ", cols$"),
         " set in CONFIG, so a variant can be matched exactly.\n",
         "  Matching on position alone would conflate a hotspot with a benign ",
         "change at the same base.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  paste(v$chrom, v$pos, toupper(v$ref), toupper(v$alt), sep = ":")
}

# Gate 1. Returns the table with normal samples and their variants removed.
germline_subtract <- function(v, type_value, min_normals, scope) {
  if (is.null(type_value) || all(is.na(type_value))) {
    return(list(variants = v, fired = FALSE,
                note = "not configured (germline_type_value is NA)"))
  }
  if (!"type" %in% names(v)) {
    stop("germline_type_value is set but cols$type is not, so no column says ",
         "which samples are normals.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_norm <- !is.na(v$type) & toupper(v$type) == toupper(type_value)
  n_norm <- dplyr::n_distinct(v$sample[is_norm])
  if (!n_norm) {
    warning("No sample has type '", type_value, "', so the germline ",
            "subtraction removed nothing. Check cols$type and ",
            "germline_type_value.", call. = FALSE)
    return(list(variants = v, fired = FALSE,
                note = sprintf("no sample has type '%s'", type_value)))
  }

  v$.key <- .variant_key(v)
  norm <- v[is_norm, , drop = FALSE]
  tum <- v[!is_norm, , drop = FALSE]

  if (scope == "matched") {
    if (!"donor" %in% names(v)) {
      stop("germline_scope is \"matched\" but cols$donor is not set, so a ",
           "normal cannot be tied to its own tumours.\n  Set cols$donor, or ",
           "set germline_scope <- \"cohort\" and read what that costs in ",
           "section 3b.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    hits <- norm %>%
      distinct(donor, .key) %>%
      mutate(.germline = TRUE)
    before <- nrow(tum)
    tum <- tum %>%
      left_join(hits, by = c("donor", ".key")) %>%
      filter(is.na(.germline)) %>%
      select(-.germline)
    covered <- dplyr::n_distinct(norm$donor)
    note <- sprintf(
      "matched: %d normal(s) covering %d donor(s); %d of %d tumour rows dropped",
      n_norm, covered, before - nrow(tum), before)
  } else if (scope == "cohort") {
    hits <- norm %>%
      count(.key, name = ".n_norm") %>%
      filter(.n_norm >= min_normals)
    before <- nrow(tum)
    tum <- tum %>% filter(!.key %in% hits$.key)
    note <- sprintf(
      "cohort: %d normal(s) as a panel; %d of %d tumour rows dropped",
      n_norm, before - nrow(tum), before)
    if (n_norm < 5) {
      warning("germline_scope is \"cohort\" with only ", n_norm, " normal(s). ",
              "One individual is hom-ref at many common SNPs, so this misses ",
              "most of them and adds that person's private variants to every ",
              "sample's blacklist. \"matched\" is the honest setting here.",
              call. = FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    stop("germline_scope must be \"matched\" or \"cohort\", not \"", scope, "\"",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  tum$.key <- NULL
  list(variants = tum, fired = TRUE, note = note, n_normals = n_norm)
}

# The sample universe for the figure and for every percentage. A normal is a
# reference, not a case: left in, it draws as an empty column and inflates the
# denominator of every pct_samples, so 6 of 8 cases reads as 66.7%, not 75%.
tumour_samples <- function(df, cols, type_value) {
  s <- trimws(as.character(df[[cols$sample]]))
  keep <- nzchar(s) & !is.na(s)
  if (!is.null(type_value) && !all(is.na(type_value)) &&
      !is.null(cols$type) && !all(is.na(cols$type)) &&
      cols$type %in% names(df)) {
    ty <- trimws(as.character(df[[cols$type]]))
    keep <- keep & !(toupper(ty) == toupper(type_value) & !is.na(ty))
  }
  sort(unique(s[keep]))
}

# Gate 2. Population allele frequency, with the freebayes AF trap guarded.
pop_af_filter <- function(v, af_col_name, max_af) {
  if (!"pop_af" %in% names(v)) {
    return(list(variants = v, fired = FALSE,
                note = "not configured (cols$pop_af is NA)"))
  }
  if (!is.null(af_col_name) && !all(is.na(af_col_name)) &&
      toupper(trimws(af_col_name)) == "AF") {
    stop("cols$pop_af is set to \"AF\", which is almost certainly NOT a ",
         "population frequency.\n  freebayes writes AF as the within-sample ",
         "allele fraction (~0.50 het, ~1.00 hom); filtering on it would ",
         "delete nearly every real variant.\n  Re-annotate with a prefix ",
         "(SnpSift annotate -name gnomad_ ...) and use that column instead.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  af <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v$pop_af))
  if (all(is.na(af))) {
    warning("cols$pop_af is set but no value in it is numeric, so the ",
            "population-frequency gate removed nothing.", call. = FALSE)
    return(list(variants = v, fired = FALSE, note = "column holds no numbers"))
  }
  before <- nrow(v)
  # NA means "not in the reference set", which for a population database is
  # evidence of rarity. Keep those rather than dropping what we cannot score.
  v <- v[is.na(af) | af <= max_af, , drop = FALSE]
  list(variants = v, fired = TRUE,
       note = sprintf("%s > %s: %d of %d rows dropped",
                      af_col_name, format(max_af), before - nrow(v), before))
}

# ---- The shared filter pipeline -----------------------------------------
# Section 1 and Section 2 must agree on what a kept variant is, so the logic
# lives here once. Returns the filtered long table plus a per-stage tally.
prepare_variants <- function(df, cols, class_map, impact_whitelist,
                             germline_type_value = NA_character_,
                             germline_min_normals = 1,
                             germline_scope = "matched",
                             max_pop_af = 0.01) {
  need <- c("sample", "gene", "consequence")
  miss <- need[vapply(cols[need],
                      function(z) is.null(z) || all(is.na(z)), logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    stop("cols$", paste(miss, collapse = ", cols$"), " must be set in CONFIG",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  absent <- setdiff(unlist(cols[need]), names(df))
  if (length(absent)) {
    stop("Column(s) not in the variant table: ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "),
         "\n  Table has: ", paste(names(df), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  keep_map <- c(sample = cols$sample, gene = cols$gene,
                consequence = cols$consequence)
  for (opt in c("impact", "protein", "chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt",
                "type", "donor", "pop_af", "ao", "ro")) {
    nm <- cols[[opt]]
    if (!is.null(nm) && !all(is.na(nm)) && nm %in% names(df)) keep_map[opt] <- nm
  }

  v <- df[, unname(keep_map), drop = FALSE]
  names(v) <- names(keep_map)

  tally <- c(rows_in = nrow(v))

  v <- v %>%
    mutate(across(any_of(c("sample", "gene", "consequence", "impact")),
                  ~ trimws(as.character(.x)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(gene), nzchar(gene), !is.na(sample), nzchar(sample))
  tally["after_blank_gene_or_sample"] <- nrow(v)

  # Consequence -> class. Unmapped terms are kept but flagged, never silently
  # folded into whichever class happens to sort first.
  v$consequence_key <- tolower(v$consequence)
  v <- left_join(v, class_map, by = "consequence_key")
  unmapped <- sort(unique(v$consequence[is.na(v$class)]))
  v$class[is.na(v$class)] <- "Unmapped"
  v$plot[is.na(v$plot)] <- FALSE

  if (!is.null(impact_whitelist) && "impact" %in% names(v)) {
    v <- v %>% filter(toupper(impact) %in% toupper(impact_whitelist))
  }
  tally["after_impact_filter"] <- nrow(v)

  # Germline gates run here, before the class filter, so the staged report
  # shows how much of the impact-passing set was inherited.
  g1 <- germline_subtract(v, germline_type_value, germline_min_normals,
                          germline_scope)
  v <- g1$variants
  tally["after_germline_subtraction"] <- nrow(v)

  g2 <- pop_af_filter(v, cols$pop_af, max_pop_af)
  v <- g2$variants
  tally["after_pop_af_filter"] <- nrow(v)

  v <- v %>% filter(plot)
  tally["after_class_plot_filter"] <- nrow(v)

  list(variants = v, tally = tally, unmapped_consequences = unmapped,
       germline = list(subtraction = g1, pop_af = g2))
}

# Per-gene recurrence summary, used for ranking and for the CSV.
summarise_genes <- function(v, n_samples_total) {
  # n_variants must count VARIANTS, not annotation rows. SnpEff emits one row
  # per transcript and one per '&'-joined consequence, so n() multiplies a
  # single variant in a many-transcript gene - and n_variants is the
  # top_n_genes tiebreak, so that inflation changes which genes get drawn.
  id <- intersect(c("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt"), names(v))
  vid <- if (length(id)) {
    do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(v[id])), sep = ":"))
  } else {
    # No coordinates mapped: the finest honest identity left is the sample,
    # the class and the protein change, if there is one.
    do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(
      v[intersect(c("class", "protein", "consequence"), names(v))])), sep = ":"))
  }
  v$.vid <- paste(v$sample, vid, sep = "@")

  # Gate 3, flag only. A germline het sits near 0.50 in every carrier.
  has_vaf <- all(c("ao", "ro") %in% names(v))
  if (has_vaf) {
    ao <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v$ao))
    ro <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v$ro))
    v$.vaf <- ifelse(is.na(ao) | is.na(ro) | (ao + ro) == 0, NA_real_,
                     ao / (ao + ro))
  }

  out <- v %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(
      n_samples        = n_distinct(sample),
      n_variants       = n_distinct(.vid),
      classes_observed = paste(sort(unique(class)), collapse = ";"),
      median_vaf       = if (has_vaf) round(stats::median(.vaf, na.rm = TRUE), 3)
                         else NA_real_,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(pct_samples = round(100 * n_samples / n_samples_total, 1)) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_samples), desc(n_variants), gene)

  if (!has_vaf) out$median_vaf <- NULL
  out
}

# ---- Load the editable inputs -------------------------------------------
class_map_raw <- read_any(class_map_file)
req_cols <- c("consequence", "class", "plot", "precedence", "color", "height")
if (!all(req_cols %in% names(class_map_raw))) {
  stop("consequence_classes.csv needs columns: ", paste(req_cols, collapse = ", "),
       call. = FALSE)
}
class_map <- class_map_raw %>%
  transmute(
    consequence_key = tolower(trimws(consequence)),
    class      = trimws(class),
    plot       = as.logical(plot),
    precedence = as.numeric(precedence),
    color      = trimws(color),
    height     = as.numeric(height)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(consequence_key), nzchar(consequence_key)) %>%
  distinct(consequence_key, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Several consequences can map to one class; collapse to a per-class style.
class_style <- class_map %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarise(precedence = min(precedence), color = dplyr::first(color),
            height = max(height), plot = any(plot), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(precedence)

whitelist <- read_patterns(whitelist_file)
blacklist <- read_patterns(blacklist_file)

say("CONFIG loaded.")
say("  consequence_classes.csv : %d terms -> %d classes (%d plotted)",
    nrow(class_map), nrow(class_style), sum(class_style$plot))
say("  gene_whitelist.txt      : %d pattern(s)%s", length(whitelist),
    if (!length(whitelist)) "   [empty - every gene is a candidate]" else "")
say("  gene_blacklist.txt      : %d pattern(s)", length(blacklist))
say("  output -> %s", out_dir)
```

# Section 0 - parse SnpEff VCFs (optional)

Skip this if you already have a long annotated variant table. Set `vcf_dir` in
CONFIG to run it. Writes `output/variants_annotated.csv.gz`, which is what
`variant_table` points at by default.

```{r section0-vcf-ingest, eval = !is.na(vcf_dir)}
stopifnot(!is.na(vcf_dir))
if (!requireNamespace("vcfR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Section 0 needs vcfR: install.packages(\"vcfR\")", call. = FALSE)
}

vcf_files <- list.files(vcf_dir, pattern = "[.]vcf([.]gz)?$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
say("Found %d VCF file(s) under %s", length(vcf_files), vcf_dir)
if (!length(vcf_files)) stop("No VCFs found. Check vcf_dir.", call. = FALSE)

# SnpEff ANN= is a comma-separated list of annotations, each one 16
# pipe-separated fields. Field order is fixed by the SnpEff spec.
ANN_FIELDS <- c("Allele", "Consequence", "Impact", "Gene_Name", "Gene_ID",
                "Feature_Type", "Transcript_ID", "Biotype", "Rank", "HGVS_c",
                "HGVS_p", "cDNA_pos", "CDS_pos", "AA_pos", "Distance", "Errors")

parse_one_vcf <- function(path) {
  nm <- basename(path)
  v <- tryCatch(vcfR::read.vcfR(path, verbose = FALSE),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(v)) {
    warning("Failed to read: ", nm, call. = FALSE)
    return(NULL)
  }
  if (nrow(v@fix) == 0) {
    warning("No variants in: ", nm, call. = FALSE)
    return(NULL)
  }

  fx <- as.data.frame(v@fix, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  rm(v)

  # A missing QUAL means unfilterable, not failed. Mutect2 and several other
  # callers write '.', and treating that as a failed filter silently discarded
  # every record in the file with a warning that blamed min_qual.
  qual <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(fx$QUAL))
  if (all(is.na(qual))) {
    message("  no numeric QUAL in ", nm,
            " (callers such as Mutect2 write '.') - min_qual not applied")
  } else {
    fx <- fx[is.na(qual) | qual >= min_qual, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (!nrow(fx)) {
    warning("No QUAL >= ", min_qual, " variants in: ", nm, call. = FALSE)
    return(NULL)
  }

  fx$ANN <- str_extract(fx$INFO, "(?<=ANN=)[^;]+")
  fx <- fx[!is.na(fx$ANN), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(fx)) {
    warning("No ANN= field in: ", nm, " - was it run through SnpEff?",
            call. = FALSE)
    return(NULL)
  }

  # AO/RO carry the within-sample allele fraction, which is what the germline
  # VAF flag reads. They live in INFO, so pull them out before INFO is dropped.
  fx$AO <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(
    str_extract(str_extract(fx$INFO, "(?<=[;\\t]AO=|^AO=)[^;]+"), "^[0-9.]+")))
  fx$RO <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(
    str_extract(str_extract(fx$INFO, "(?<=[;\\t]RO=|^RO=)[^;]+"), "^[0-9.]+")))

  out <- fx %>%
    select(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER, AO, RO, ANN) %>%
    mutate(ANN = str_split(ANN, ",")) %>%
    unnest(ANN)

  f <- str_split_fixed(out$ANN, "\\|", n = length(ANN_FIELDS))
  colnames(f) <- ANN_FIELDS
  out <- bind_cols(select(out, -ANN), as.data.frame(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

  # SnpEff joins co-occurring consequences with '&'; one row each.
  out <- out %>%
    mutate(Consequence = str_split(Consequence, "&")) %>%
    unnest(Consequence) %>%
    mutate(Consequence = trimws(Consequence)) %>%
    filter(nzchar(Consequence))

  out$File <- nm
  for (fld in names(filename_fields)) {
    m <- str_match(nm, filename_fields[[fld]])
    out[[fld]] <- if (all(is.na(m))) NA_character_
                  else if (ncol(m) >= 2) m[1, 2] else m[1, 1]
  }
  out
}

parsed <- lapply(vcf_files, function(f) {
  say("  parsing %s", basename(f))
  res <- parse_one_vcf(f)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  res
})

variants_annotated <- bind_rows(parsed)
rm(parsed); gc(verbose = FALSE)

if (!nrow(variants_annotated)) {
  stop("Parsed 0 annotated variants from ", length(vcf_files), " file(s).",
       call. = FALSE)
}

ann_out <- file.path(out_dir, "variants_annotated.csv.gz")
utils::write.csv(variants_annotated, gzfile(ann_out), row.names = FALSE,
                 na = "")

say("")
say("Parsed %d annotation rows across %d sample(s).",
    nrow(variants_annotated), n_distinct(variants_annotated$SampleID))
say("Wrote %s", ann_out)
say("Set variant_table to that path (it already is, by default), then run Section 1.")
```

---

# Section 1 - candidate genes

Reads the variant table, applies the impact / class / whitelist / blacklist /
recurrence filters, and writes `gene_list.csv` for you to review and edit.

**If `gene_list.csv` already exists it is not overwritten** - the new table goes
to `gene_list_draft.csv` instead, so a re-run to pick up whitelist edits never
destroys manual work. Diff the two and merge by hand.

```{r section1-candidate-genes}
raw <- read_any(variant_table)
say("Read %s", variant_table)
say("  %d rows, %d columns", nrow(raw), ncol(raw))

prep <- prepare_variants(raw, cols, class_map, impact_whitelist,
                         germline_type_value, germline_min_normals,
                         germline_scope, max_pop_af)
v <- prep$variants
t1 <- prep$tally

samples_all <- tumour_samples(raw, cols, germline_type_value)
n_samples_total <- length(samples_all)

stage_line <- function(label, kept, prev = NA) {
  say("  %-34s %8d%s", label, kept,
      if (is.na(prev)) "" else sprintf("   (-%d)", prev - kept))
}
say("")
say("Variant rows after each stage:")
stage_line("read in", t1[["rows_in"]])
stage_line("non-blank gene and sample", t1[["after_blank_gene_or_sample"]],
           t1[["rows_in"]])
stage_line(sprintf("impact in {%s}",
                   if (is.null(impact_whitelist)) "any"
                   else paste(impact_whitelist, collapse = ",")),
           t1[["after_impact_filter"]], t1[["after_blank_gene_or_sample"]])
stage_line("germline subtraction", t1[["after_germline_subtraction"]],
           t1[["after_impact_filter"]])
stage_line("population AF", t1[["after_pop_af_filter"]],
           t1[["after_germline_subtraction"]])
stage_line("consequence class plotted", t1[["after_class_plot_filter"]],
           t1[["after_pop_af_filter"]])

# Say plainly whether anything germline-aware actually happened. A gate that
# is configured wrongly and a gate that is off look identical in the counts
# above, and the difference decides whether this figure means anything.
say("")
say("Germline gates:")
say("  subtraction   %s", prep$germline$subtraction$note)
say("  population AF %s", prep$germline$pop_af$note)
if (!prep$germline$subtraction$fired && !prep$germline$pop_af$fired) {
  say("")
  say("  WARNING: no germline gate fired, so this panel is ranked by recurrence")
  say("  across tumour-only calls. Inherited variants recur in every sample")
  say("  that carries them, so common polymorphisms can outrank real drivers.")
  say("  Configure section 3b, or read the figure as 'variants', not 'somatic'.")
}

if (length(prep$unmapped_consequences)) {
  say("")
  say("NOTE: %d consequence term(s) are not in consequence_classes.csv and were",
      length(prep$unmapped_consequences))
  say("      therefore dropped. Add a row for any you want plotted:")
  for (u in head(prep$unmapped_consequences, 30)) say("        %s", u)
  if (length(prep$unmapped_consequences) > 30) {
    say("        ... and %d more", length(prep$unmapped_consequences) - 30)
  }
}

if (!nrow(v)) {
  stop("No variants survived the impact/class filters. Loosen impact_whitelist ",
       "or set more classes to plot=TRUE in consequence_classes.csv.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- gene whitelist / blacklist -----------------------------------------
genes_present <- sort(unique(v$gene))
wl_hit <- match_patterns(genes_present, whitelist)
bl_hit <- match_patterns(genes_present, blacklist)

gene_flags <- tibble(
  gene = genes_present,
  matched_whitelist_pattern = wl_hit,
  matched_blacklist_pattern = bl_hit
)

# An empty whitelist means "consider every gene".
keep_wl <- if (length(whitelist)) !is.na(gene_flags$matched_whitelist_pattern) else TRUE
dropped_wl <- gene_flags$gene[!keep_wl]
gene_flags <- gene_flags[keep_wl, , drop = FALSE]

# The blacklist always wins.
dropped_bl <- gene_flags$gene[!is.na(gene_flags$matched_blacklist_pattern)]
gene_flags <- gene_flags[is.na(gene_flags$matched_blacklist_pattern), , drop = FALSE]

v <- v %>% filter(gene %in% gene_flags$gene)

name_list <- function(x, n = 12) {
  if (!length(x)) return("")
  paste0("   ", paste(head(x, n), collapse = ", "),
         if (length(x) > n) sprintf(", ... (+%d)", length(x) - n) else "")
}
say("")
say("  %-34s %8d", "genes seen in surviving variants", length(genes_present))
if (length(whitelist)) {
  say("  %-34s %8d%s", "not matched by whitelist", -length(dropped_wl),
      name_list(dropped_wl))
}
say("  %-34s %8d%s", "dropped by blacklist", -length(dropped_bl),
    name_list(dropped_bl))

# ---- recurrence ---------------------------------------------------------
gene_tbl <- summarise_genes(v, n_samples_total) %>%
  left_join(gene_flags, by = "gene")

n_before_rec <- nrow(gene_tbl)
gene_tbl <- gene_tbl %>% filter(n_samples >= min_samples_mutated)
say("  %-34s %8d", sprintf("altered in < %d sample(s)", min_samples_mutated),
    -(n_before_rec - nrow(gene_tbl)))

if (!is.na(top_n_genes) && nrow(gene_tbl) > top_n_genes) {
  say("  %-34s %8d", sprintf("beyond top_n_genes = %d", top_n_genes),
      -(nrow(gene_tbl) - top_n_genes))
  gene_tbl <- gene_tbl[seq_len(top_n_genes), , drop = FALSE]
}
say("  %-34s %8d", "GENES IN THE CANDIDATE PANEL", nrow(gene_tbl))

# Whitelist patterns that caught nothing are almost always a typo - but on a
# broad panel most patterns legitimately match nothing, so keep this short.
if (length(whitelist)) {
  unused <- setdiff(whitelist, unique(stats::na.omit(wl_hit)))
  if (length(unused)) {
    say("")
    say("NOTE: %d of %d whitelist pattern(s) matched no gene with a plottable",
        length(unused), length(whitelist))
    say("      variant. A typo, or simply not altered in this cohort:")
    say("     %s", trimws(name_list(unused, 20)))
  }
}

gene_out <- gene_tbl %>%
  transmute(
    include = TRUE,
    gene,
    n_samples,
    pct_samples,
    n_variants,
    classes_observed,
    matched_whitelist_pattern,
    notes = ""
  )

# Gate 3 is advisory, so it rides along for review rather than filtering.
# A gene whose median sits near 0.50 across every carrier is worth a look.
if ("median_vaf" %in% names(gene_tbl)) {
  gene_out$median_vaf <- gene_tbl$median_vaf[match(gene_out$gene, gene_tbl$gene)]
}

target <- gene_csv
if (file.exists(gene_csv)) {
  target <- file.path(dirname(gene_csv), "gene_list_draft.csv")
  say("")
  say("%s already exists and was NOT overwritten.", basename(gene_csv))
  say("Wrote the new table to %s instead - diff and merge by hand.",
      basename(target))
}
write_csv_std(gene_out, target)
say("")
say("Wrote %s (%d gene(s)).", target, nrow(gene_out))
say("Review it, set include=FALSE or delete rows, add genes by name, then run Section 2.")
```

---

# Section 2 - build the oncoprint

Reads `gene_list.csv`, keeps `include = TRUE` rows, and re-derives each gene's
alterations from the variant table. The CSV stores only metadata, not the
variants, which is what makes a hand-edit actually take effect.

A gene you typed in by hand needs only `include` and `gene`; the recurrence
columns are looked up and written back into the CSV for you, and only genuinely
blank cells are filled - anything you typed, `notes` included, is left alone.

```{r section2-oncoprint}
if (!file.exists(gene_csv)) {
  stop(basename(gene_csv), " not found. Run Section 1 first, then review it.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

gene_in <- read_any(gene_csv)
if (!all(c("include", "gene") %in% names(gene_in))) {
  stop(basename(gene_csv), " must have at least 'include' and 'gene' columns.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

gene_in$gene <- trimws(as.character(gene_in$gene))
gene_in <- gene_in[nzchar(gene_in$gene) & !is.na(gene_in$gene), , drop = FALSE]
inc <- as.logical(gene_in$include)
inc[is.na(inc)] <- FALSE
genes_wanted <- unique(gene_in$gene[inc])

say("%s: %d row(s), %d with include=TRUE", basename(gene_csv), nrow(gene_in),
    length(genes_wanted))
if (!length(genes_wanted)) {
  stop("No rows with include=TRUE in ", basename(gene_csv), call. = FALSE)
}

raw <- read_any(variant_table)
prep <- prepare_variants(raw, cols, class_map, impact_whitelist,
                         germline_type_value, germline_min_normals,
                         germline_scope, max_pop_af)

# Note: the gene whitelist/blacklist are deliberately NOT applied here. The CSV
# is the source of truth at this stage, so a gene you added by hand is honoured
# even if the blacklist would have caught it.
v <- prep$variants %>% filter(toupper(gene) %in% toupper(genes_wanted))

found <- unique(v$gene)
absent <- genes_wanted[!toupper(genes_wanted) %in% toupper(found)]
if (length(absent)) {
  say("")
  say("%d gene(s) in the CSV have no plottable variant in the table and are",
      length(absent))
  say("  skipped rather than drawn as empty rows:")
  for (g in absent) say("    %s", g)
}
if (!nrow(v)) {
  stop("None of the included genes have a plottable variant.", call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- samples ------------------------------------------------------------
samples_all <- tumour_samples(raw, cols, germline_type_value)

sample_annot <- NULL
if (!is.na(sample_annotation_csv) && file.exists(sample_annotation_csv)) {
  sample_annot <- read_any(sample_annotation_csv)
  names(sample_annot)[1] <- "sample"
  sample_annot$sample <- trimws(as.character(sample_annot$sample))
  extra <- setdiff(samples_all, sample_annot$sample)
  if (length(extra)) {
    say("")
    say("NOTE: %d sample(s) in the variant table are missing from %s:",
        length(extra), basename(sample_annotation_csv))
    for (s in head(extra, 12)) say("        %s", s)
    if (length(extra) > 12) say("        ... and %d more", length(extra) - 12)
    say("      They are still drawn, with blank annotation.")
  }
  dup <- unique(sample_annot$sample[duplicated(sample_annot$sample)])
  if (length(dup)) {
    # Left unchecked this fans out the annotation join below and oncoPrint
    # fails with an error that says nothing about this file.
    stop(basename(sample_annotation_csv), " has duplicate sample ID(s): ",
         paste(dup, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  # The annotation file sets the universe, so a sequenced-but-unaltered sample
  # still gets its column. It does NOT set the order - that comes from
  # oncoPrint's memo-sort unless you set sample_order.
  samples_all <- union(sample_annot$sample, samples_all)
}

if (!is.null(sample_order)) {
  missing_req <- setdiff(sample_order, samples_all)
  if (length(missing_req)) {
    say("NOTE: sample_order names %d sample(s) not in the data; ignored: %s",
        length(missing_req), paste(head(missing_req, 8), collapse = ", "))
  }
  samples_all <- intersect(sample_order, samples_all)
}

# ---- matrix -------------------------------------------------------------
# One cell per gene x sample, holding every alteration class seen there, most
# severe first, joined with ';' - the format oncoPrint expects.
prec <- setNames(class_style$precedence, class_style$class)

# Rank and draw from the same sample universe. Ranking over all of v while
# dividing by the drawn samples put impossible percentages into gene_list.csv
# and ordered the rows by a cohort the figure does not show.
v_plot <- v %>% filter(sample %in% samples_all)

cell_tbl <- v_plot %>%
  mutate(.p = prec[class]) %>%
  distinct(gene, sample, class, .p) %>%
  arrange(gene, sample, .p, class) %>%
  group_by(gene, sample) %>%
  summarise(value = paste(unique(class), collapse = ";"), .groups = "drop")

gene_rank <- summarise_genes(v_plot, length(samples_all))
genes_ordered <- if (!is.null(gene_order)) {
  intersect(gene_order, gene_rank$gene)
} else {
  gene_rank$gene
}

mat <- matrix("", nrow = length(genes_ordered), ncol = length(samples_all),
              dimnames = list(genes_ordered, samples_all))
idx <- cbind(match(cell_tbl$gene, genes_ordered),
             match(cell_tbl$sample, samples_all))
ok <- !is.na(idx[, 1]) & !is.na(idx[, 2])
mat[idx[ok, , drop = FALSE]] <- cell_tbl$value[ok]

say("")
say("Matrix: %d gene(s) x %d sample(s); %d altered cell(s) (%.1f%% filled).",
    nrow(mat), ncol(mat), sum(nzchar(mat)),
    100 * sum(nzchar(mat)) / length(mat))

# ---- alter_fun ----------------------------------------------------------
classes_drawn <- class_style %>%
  filter(plot, class %in% unique(v_plot$class)) %>%
  # Big bars first so small ones land on top. Within a height tie the less
  # severe class is drawn first, so the more severe one stays visible.
  arrange(desc(height), desc(precedence))

# Two plotted classes at the same height draw identical rectangles, so wherever
# they co-occur the second one paints the first out completely and the figure
# silently disagrees with the matrix CSV and the barplots.
.tied <- classes_drawn$height[duplicated(classes_drawn$height)]
if (length(.tied)) {
  tied_classes <- classes_drawn$class[classes_drawn$height %in% .tied]
  warning("These plotted classes share a height, so whichever is drawn second ",
          "hides the other wherever they co-occur in one cell: ",
          paste(tied_classes, collapse = ", "),
          ".\n  Give each a distinct height in ", basename(class_map_file),
          call. = FALSE)
}

# force() matters: without it every closure would capture the loop's last value.
make_rect <- function(fill, frac) {
  force(fill); force(frac)
  function(x, y, w, h) {
    grid.rect(x, y, w - unit(0.4, "mm"), h * frac - unit(0.4, "mm"),
              gp = gpar(fill = fill, col = NA))
  }
}

alter_fun <- list(
  background = function(x, y, w, h) {
    grid.rect(x, y, w - unit(0.4, "mm"), h - unit(0.4, "mm"),
              gp = gpar(fill = background_col, col = NA))
  }
)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(classes_drawn))) {
  alter_fun[[classes_drawn$class[i]]] <-
    make_rect(classes_drawn$color[i], classes_drawn$height[i])
}
col_vec <- setNames(classes_drawn$color, classes_drawn$class)

# ---- top annotation -----------------------------------------------------
top_annot <- NULL
if (!is.null(sample_annot)) {
  ann_df <- data.frame(sample = samples_all, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(sample_annot, by = "sample")
  ann_cols <- setdiff(names(ann_df), "sample")
  ann_cols <- ann_cols[vapply(ann_df[ann_cols],
                              function(z) any(!is.na(z)), logical(1))]
  if (length(ann_cols)) {
    ann_df <- ann_df[, ann_cols, drop = FALSE]
    pal <- c("#1F78B4", "#33A02C", "#FF7F00", "#6A3D9A", "#B2182B", "#A6761D",
             "#E7298A", "#66C2A5", "#FFD92F", "#8DA0CB", "#4D4D4D", "#BDBDBD")
    ann_colors <- list()
    for (cn in ann_cols) {
      if (!is.null(annotation_colors[[cn]])) {
        ann_colors[[cn]] <- annotation_colors[[cn]]
      } else {
        lv <- sort(unique(stats::na.omit(as.character(ann_df[[cn]]))))
        if (length(lv)) {
          ann_colors[[cn]] <- setNames(
            rep(pal, length.out = length(lv))[seq_along(lv)], lv)
        }
      }
    }
    top_annot <- HeatmapAnnotation(df = ann_df, col = ann_colors,
                                   annotation_name_side = "left",
                                   na_col = "#FFFFFF")
  }
}

# ---- draw ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Derive into locals. Assigning back into fig_w/fig_h would leave them numeric
# after the first run, so the documented "re-run Section 2 only" loop would
# reuse the first figure's size and clip a larger matrix.
.fig_w <- if (is.na(fig_w)) max(7, 2.8 + ncol(mat) * cell_w / 25.4 + 2.2) else fig_w
.fig_h <- if (is.na(fig_h)) max(4, 1.6 + nrow(mat) * cell_h / 25.4 + 1.4) else fig_h

op <- oncoPrint(
  mat,
  alter_fun       = alter_fun,
  alter_fun_is_vectorized = TRUE,
  col             = col_vec,
  get_type        = function(x) strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]],
  column_order    = if (is.null(sample_order)) NULL else samples_all,
  # mat is already built in the order we want, and oncoPrint's own row sort
  # disagrees just often enough to make the percent column non-monotonic.
  row_order       = seq_len(nrow(mat)),
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  remove_empty_columns = FALSE,
  remove_empty_rows    = FALSE,
  # pct_side is passed unconditionally: show_pct = FALSE already hides the
  # column, whereas pct_side = NULL reaches oncoPrint's own `if` and dies on a
  # zero-length condition.
  pct_side        = "left",
  show_pct        = show_pct,
  top_annotation  = top_annot,
  width           = unit(ncol(mat) * cell_w, "mm"),
  height          = unit(nrow(mat) * cell_h, "mm"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Alteration")
)

pdf_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(out_name, ".pdf"))
pdf(pdf_path, width = .fig_w, height = .fig_h)
draw(op, column_title = plot_title, merge_legend = TRUE,
     heatmap_legend_side = "right", annotation_legend_side = "right")
dev.off()
say("Wrote %s", pdf_path)

if (write_png) {
  png_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(out_name, ".png"))
  png(png_path, width = .fig_w, height = .fig_h, units = "in", res = png_dpi,
      type = if (capabilities("cairo")) "cairo" else getOption("bitmapType"))
  draw(op, column_title = plot_title, merge_legend = TRUE,
       heatmap_legend_side = "right", annotation_legend_side = "right")
  dev.off()
  say("Wrote %s", png_path)
}

mat_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(out_name, "_matrix.csv"))
write_csv_std(data.frame(gene = rownames(mat), mat, check.names = FALSE),
              mat_path)
say("Wrote %s", mat_path)

long_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(out_name, "_long.csv"))
write_csv_std(v %>% select(-any_of(c("consequence_key", "plot", "precedence",
                                     "color", "height"))), long_path)
say("Wrote %s", long_path)

# ---- fill blank metadata back into gene_list.csv ------------------------
# Only genuinely empty cells, so a hand-typed row gains its recurrence numbers
# without anything you wrote being touched.
fillable <- c("n_samples", "pct_samples", "n_variants", "classes_observed")
look <- gene_rank %>% select(gene, all_of(intersect(fillable, names(gene_rank))))
changed <- 0L
for (cn in intersect(fillable, names(look))) {
  if (!cn %in% names(gene_in)) gene_in[[cn]] <- NA
  m <- match(toupper(gene_in$gene), toupper(look$gene))
  blank <- is.na(gene_in[[cn]]) |
    (is.character(gene_in[[cn]]) & !nzchar(as.character(gene_in[[cn]])))
  hit <- blank & !is.na(m)
  if (any(hit)) {
    gene_in[[cn]][hit] <- look[[cn]][m[hit]]
    changed <- changed + sum(hit)
  }
}
if (changed > 0L) {
  write_csv_std(gene_in, gene_csv)
  say("Filled %d blank metadata cell(s) back into %s.", changed,
      basename(gene_csv))
}

say("")
say("Done. %d gene(s) x %d sample(s).", nrow(mat), ncol(mat))
```
